assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major transformation in measuring and explaining unequal opportunity, with unusually broad influence on research and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the mobility research program; Friedman is a principal collaborator in building and exploiting linked administrative-data evidence.
assessment.maturity: The research program is extensive, replicated in related settings, and has reshaped empirical work on mobility over more than a decade.
uncertainties: The underlying data infrastructure and research program involve a wider set of important contributors than three laureate places can recognize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Provides compelling evidence and an influential framework for understanding how trade, technology, and tasks reshape local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson have distinct and central roles in the trade-shock and labour-demand evidence assembled under this contribution.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large subsequent literature and remain central to research on labour-market adjustment.
uncertainties: Separating the contribution from adjacent literatures on technological change and trade adjustment is inherently difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of evidence and theory establishing that early-life conditions have durable consequences for health, education, and economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond provided formative empirical evidence using policy and environmental variation, while Cunha made central contributions to the dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: The conclusion is supported by a broad, long-running body of quasi-experimental and longitudinal research.
uncertainties: The candidate combines empirical early-life work and structural skill-formation research whose precise boundaries are broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance-market theory with credible empirical measurement has materially changed health, public, and applied microeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie each made recognizable foundational contributions to theory, measurement, and empirical analysis of selection.
assessment.maturity: The work is deeply embedded in a mature applied literature and has informed the analysis of insurance design.
uncertainties: Adverse selection is a large literature with several consequential contributors outside the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs made discrimination measurable in a transparent and policy-relevant way, with enduring influence across applied economics.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan produced the landmark modern audit study; Charles is an important contributor to the broader economic analysis of racial disparities and discrimination.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been widely adopted, refined, and extended across labour and housing markets.
uncertainties: Audit designs identify discrimination at particular margins and do not by themselves resolve all mechanisms behind aggregate disparities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of employer market power has redirected labour economics toward a more realistic account of wage setting and labour-market institutions.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied the foundational monopsony framework, and Naidu has been central to its modern empirical and institutional development.
assessment.maturity: A large recent empirical literature has confirmed the importance of imperfect competition in many labour markets.
uncertainties: The evidence and policy implications remain heterogeneous across labour-market settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a tractable and influential account of how distorted input allocation can generate large productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow developed a defining quantitative application, while Restuccia made central contributions to the broader misallocation literature.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively used in growth, development, and firm-level research.
uncertainties: Quantitative estimates can be sensitive to modeling assumptions and to whether observed dispersion represents distortions or productive heterogeneity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods provided an essential bridge between dynamic economic theory and empirical analysis of individual decisions.
assessment.attribution: Rust established a seminal structural approach; Keane and Eckstein made major contributions to estimation and substantive dynamic-choice applications.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, influential, and used throughout labour, industrial organization, and public economics.
uncertainties: The contribution overlaps with a wide methodological literature, and structural conclusions depend on maintained model specification.
